workflows.title: WF2 Compromised endpoint
workflows.description: Scope one host: what ran, how it got in, whether it persists, whether it calls out, whether it spread.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead B, or WF1 Step 5 pointed at a host.  
**You need:** the host name, and the user if you have it.  
**Goal:** decide whether to contain the host and find where the attacker went next. About 10 minutes.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

evidence.title: Detections on this host
evidence.expr: sum by (severity, detection_name, technique_id, action, user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | event_type="Detection" [$__range]))

card.look: every detection on the host, worst first.
card.bad: high or critical with action `allowed`, or several tactics in a row (Execution, Persistence, Discovery, Credential Access).
card.if_bad: go to Step 2 to see how it started.
card.if_clean: a single low or medium detection that was blocked or quarantined. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Suspicious process chain on this host
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | event_type="Detection" | line_format "{{.parent_process}} -> {{.process}}   [{{.technique_id}}]  {{.cmdline}}" | keep service_name

card.bad: an Office app (`excel.exe`, `winword.exe`, `outlook.exe`) starting `powershell`, `cmd`, `rundll32` or `mshta`; `-enc` or `-w hidden` on the command line.
card.if_bad: Office as the parent means a malicious attachment. Go to Step 3.
card.if_clean: the chain starts from explorer or a known updater.

steps.title: Did it come in by email?

evidence.title: Mail to this user from new domains
evidence.expr: sum by (sender_domain, subject, attachment, verdict, domain_age_days) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-email"} | json | recipient=~"$user@.*" | domain_age_days < 30 [$__range]))

evidence.title: Everyone who got mail from new domains (click to open WF1)
evidence.expr: topk(40, sum by (recipient_user, sender_domain, verdict) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-email"} | json | domain_age_days < 30 | label_format recipient_user=`{{ regexReplaceAll "@.*" .recipient "" }}` [$__range])))

card.look: mail the user received from domains younger than 30 days, then everyone else who got the same mail.
card.bad: a delivered message from a new lookalike domain with a macro attachment (`.xlsm`, `.docm`) shortly before Step 2.
card.if_bad: every other delivered recipient is a potential second victim. Click each one to open WF1.
card.if_clean: nothing from a new domain. The entry point was something else (web, USB, VPN). Keep going.

evidence.title: Persistence on this host
evidence.expr: sum by (detection_name, technique_id, process, cmdline) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | technique_id=~"T1053.*|T1543.*|T1547.*" [$__range]))

card.look: scheduled tasks, services and run keys created on the host.
card.bad: `schtasks /create`, a new service or a run key pointing at a user-writable path (AppData, Temp, ProgramData).
card.if_bad: note the task name and binary for the eradication list.
card.if_clean: no persistence found. Containment may be enough.

steps.title: Is it talking to command and control?

evidence.title: Small outbound sessions per destination (beacons are flat lines)
evidence.expr: topk(5, sum by (dst_domain) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | src_host="$host" | dst_zone="internet" | bytes < 2000 [5m])))

evidence.title: New domains this host resolved
evidence.expr: sum by (query, domain_age_days, category) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-dns"} | json | host="$host" | domain_age_days < 30 [$__range]))

card.look: small, regular outbound connections per destination, and new domains the host resolved.
card.bad: one destination every minute with almost identical size (a flat line), or a domain under 30 days old.
card.if_bad: block the domain and IP at the firewall and DNS. Add them to the case.
card.if_clean: outbound traffic is bursty and goes to known SaaS.

evidence.title: Explicit-credential logons to other hosts
evidence.help: 4648 with a different account. Personal adm- accounts via runas are excluded.

card.look: three counters for movement off this host.
card.if_bad: open [[WF3 Lateral movement from this host]].
card.if_clean: all green. The attacker probably stayed on this host.

links.label: WF3 Lateral movement from this host

evidence.title: Already contained?
evidence.help: Orange 0 = not contained yet. Green = an analyst already contained it.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Contain the host** if Step 1 had an allowed high/critical detection **and** Step 2 or Step 5 was bad.

**Do these now:**
1. Network-contain the host in EDR. Do not power it off; memory is evidence.
2. Block the C2 domain and IP from Step 5.
3. Purge the lure email from every mailbox in Step 3.
4. Add the persistence items from Step 4 to the eradication list.

**Then go to:**
- [[WF3 Lateral movement from this host]] if any Step 6 counter was red
- [[WF1 for the user]] to check the account
- [[WF4 Data exfiltration]]
- [[Case timeline for the host]]

links.label: WF3 Lateral movement from this host

also.say: Movement off this host. Run WF3 from here.

rule.close_if_false: No containment needed. Close the lead.
